chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Ross the doorman and the bell for live ones at the Nest Club
summary: A former Black Elite Giants ballplayer, Ross, stood outside and rang a bell when customers arrived so the band would strike up.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Ross told me that, Ross who was a great ballplayer with the Black Elite Giants, which preceded the Black Yankees. One of the great Black ballplayers. He was a great ballplayer. He never did make the Big Leagues, because there was no Blacks in the Big Leagues. And he was the

At the Nest Club. See, he would stand up outside, and... I saw him for quite a few years out there, rain or snow. In the wintertime he had this big, long coat like them doormen have in front of the Waldorf Astoria and in them other clubs. He would just stand out there, and lead the people in.

Now, they had a secret. In the Nest Club, nobody would be down there. We'd be just sitting down and waiting for a live one to come. Johnny Carey and Mal Frazier would have some women, they'd be talkin' to some hustlers, all sleazy looking people, lookin' real wise -- night people. And Ross would be upstairs. And they had a bell up there. So when somebody got out of a cab or a live one would come in a party of two or four, Ross would press the button. When he pressed that button, ZING-ZING-ZING-ZING, that means that some live one's coming. And the band would strike up. Right away the piano player, whoever's got a horn... They ain't waitin' for the whole band. Just start playing. That means you run and you'd get something, somebody would be coming out of the men's room, we're sitting down talking -- you know, you're relaxed. But you jump up and you start this music.
